title: AfD's Saxony-Anhalt Surge and a Fragile Recovery Put Merz's Germany to the… · 09 Sep
keywords: AfD, Saxony-Anhalt, Friedrich Merz, Germany politics, far-right, German economy, inflation Germany, GDP Germany, European Union, coalition government, eastern Germany, Bundesbank, cost of living, EU fiscal policy
notes: Germany's far-right Alternative für Deutschland has secured a striking 43.8% in Saxony-Anhalt, delivering a political shock that deepens pressure on Chancellor Friedrich Merz and his federal coalition. The result arrives against a backdrop of modestly improving economic data, yet inflation continues to climb toward 2.9% and household budgets remain under strain. The combination of political turbulence and an uneven recovery poses a defining test for Europe's largest economy and, by extension, for the European Union itself.
